fix: In bryophyte (moss) descriptions, 'capsule' means the sporophyte capsule (PO_0025094 sporangium), not PO_0030091 capsule fruit. The words 'urns', 'opercula', 'setae' and 'spores' nearby give it away.
reason: Fissidens is a moss; its capsule is a sporangium, not a fruit. The quality (erect or inclined position) is right.
'Drupe ... greenish' means the fruit is approximately green.
'bracts absent' means bracts are not present.

fix: In '<colour>-tomentose' (whitish-tomentose, fulvous-pubescent) the colour belongs to the hairs (tomentum), not to the organ. Read it as: organ is tomentose, and the hairs on it are coloured.
reason: The pedicels carry whitish hairs; the pedicel surface itself is not said to be white.

fix: 'filaments <quality>' should map to the filament (PO_0009067), not be widened to the whole stamen.
reason: The flora says 'filaments ... red or mauve'; the anthers may differ in colour.
'Petals ovate-lanceolate' is a shape continuum from ovate to lanceolate, recorded correctly.
'inflorescence ... usually many-flowered': many flowers in the inflorescence, with the 'usually' kept.
The primary bract is longer than the inflorescence, with 'usually' kept.

fix: In 'X to Y from an A or B base', A and B describe the leaf base; X and Y describe the whole leaf.
reason: Ovate or oblong is the shape of the leaf base. The leaf as a whole is lanceolate to linear-lanceolate.
The inflorescence is glabrous or sparsely glandular-puberulent; the alternatives are recorded correctly.
'Lamina oblong-ovate' is a shape continuum from oblong to ovate.
The elliptic-oblong part of the shape range is recorded correctly; 'to obovate' is a further alternative, so nothing recorded is false.
'Inflorescences few-flowered': few flowers in the inflorescence.

target: PO_0008021 tertiary leaf vein, inconspicuous (PATO_0000464), not negated
fix: '<part> not evident' means the part is inconspicuous (not negated). The negation is part of the meaning, not a negation of 'inconspicuous', and the bearer is the named part, not the whole blade.
reason: The flora says the tertiary veins are not visible. The annotation says instead that the lamina is NOT inconspicuous, which is the opposite of what the flora means.
The shape range from narrowly linear to broadly ovate is recorded with its 'narrowly'/'broadly' qualifiers; 'or rarely subrotund' is a further alternative.

fix: 'lower 1 or 2 ..., upper ones ...' splits the bracts by position. Each half needs its position slot (pattern 04), or the two statements contradict each other.
reason: Only the upper bracts are shorter than the inflorescence; the lower 1 or 2 are longer. Without 'upper' the statement is false.
'Berry reddish': the fruit is approximately red. 'Sometimes yellow' is a separate alternative.
The sepal apex is sometimes puberulent; the bearer is narrowed correctly and 'sometimes' is kept.

target: apex of the leaflet (narrow the bearer as in A01377; PO has no leaflet-apex class in the lexicon, so use the apex as the scope)
fix: 'apex obtuse or acute' after a description of the leaflet must narrow the bearer to the apex (bearer_scope), not give the apex shape to the whole leaflet.
reason: Obtuse or acute describes the leaflet tip, not the shape of the whole leaflet.

fix: 'upper glume' and 'lower glume' have their own PO classes (PO_0006004, PO_0006002); map to them instead of the general glume.
reason: Only the upper glume is acute or acuminate; the lower glume is blunt. 'Glume acute' is false for the lower one.
Nutlet pale brown: mapping 'pale brown' to 'light grayish brown' is a curated choice (decision B3) and is correct.
The leaves are coriaceous (leathery).

fix: 'deltoid' should map to PATO_0001875 triangular. Here the value was dropped and only the general 'shape' was kept, which says nothing.
reason: The young-plant whole (stage) slot is right, but the annotation has no shape value, so 'deltoid' is lost.
Stigmas are 1.3–1.7 mm long.

fix: 'the 3 lower <parts> X' needs the position slot (and the count). Without it, X is said of all anthers.
reason: Only the 3 lower anthers are beaked; in this genus the other anthers differ.
The leaf blades are 0.3–6 cm wide.
The petals are cuneate or sometimes spatulate. Only the 'sometimes' on the second alternative is lost, which is minor.
The leaf blade apex is rounded. Mapping it to obtuse (synonym 'roundish') on the leaf lamina tip is acceptable.
There are 5 petals.
The style is shorter than the ovary.
